title: The Nina Steiner Guide to Leasing Short-Term Office and Storage Space for Los Angeles Olympics | User | dailytimesleader.com
text:
Nina Steiner, a Los Angeles tenant rep broker, announces expert short-term office and storage solutions for companies supporting the 2028 Olympics. Her streamlined approach helps vendors, sponsors, and event teams quickly secure flexible, professional workspaces across the city.
Los Angeles, CA, California, United States, July 24, 2025 -- With the 2028 Summer Olympics approaching, businesses and sports teams connected to planning, logistics, sponsorship, and event production are moving quickly to secure office space in Los Angeles. The need for flexible, short-term offices has never been greater, as companies recognize that a professional base is essential for success during the Games.
Learn More About Short Term Space Here https://tenantrepla.com/temporary-office-space-in-los-angeles-for-2028-olympics/
“Every Olympic space requirement is unique, but one thing is constant: teams needs a place to land, focus, and organize. You shouldn’t have to commit to years of rent just to get your work done for a few critical months,” said Nina Steiner, tenant rep broker at Saxum West and specialist in Olympic-related office and storage leasing.
Short-term office space solutions are helping vendors, sponsors, contractors, and media groups operate more efficiently across Los Angeles. These temporary offices allow teams to support on-site managers, coordinate with local partners, and keep projects organized without the limitations of hotels or makeshift spaces. Businesses benefit from being close to the action, reducing travel expenses, and having access to secure, private environments.
A variety of office types are available to meet Olympic needs. Move-in-ready suites, fully furnished with Wi-Fi and utilities, provide immediate solutions for teams who need to get started fast. Flexible lease terms—ranging from month-to-month to twelve months—offer the adaptability that Olympic projects demand. Teams seeking more space or privacy can access standalone offices with dedicated entrances, conference rooms, and parking.
“Choosing the right location can make or break a project. My clients appreciate options near Downtown LA for venue access, in Culver City for creative work, Santa Monica for tech and sponsor teams, and Inglewood for stadium-focused operations,” Nina Steiner added.
The leasing process isn’t always simple. Many landlords don’t offer true short-term flexibility, and not every property comes with essential services included. Steiner’s expertise helps clients avoid costly mistakes by focusing on offices that offer secure access, included amenities, and the ability to scale up or down as needs evolve.
Drawing on her background in live television production, Steiner brings a unique problem-solving approach to commercial real estate. She has guided numerous Olympic vendors and support firms through tight timelines and complex requirements, always with a focus on understanding their real needs.
“My job is to take the uncertainty out of the process,” said Steiner. “Clients get a tailored shortlist of real options within a day. I handle the details—from tours and negotiations to paperwork—so they can stay focused on their Olympic goals.”
To get started, Steiner asks for the basics: team size, preferred locations, start date, duration, must-have features, and budget. From there, she does the rest—delivering a fast, frictionless office solution that keeps each Olympic project moving forward.
